title: The truncated weighted sum of the scale-invariant process is exponentially distributed
source_title: On Arratia's coupling and the Dirichlet law for the factors of a random integer

standard_prerequisites.name: The truncated weighted sum
standard_prerequisites.statement: I_t is the sum of the second coordinates of the points of the scale-invariant process whose first coordinate exceeds t.
standard_prerequisites.use: It is the random variable whose law is identified.

standard_prerequisites.name: Campbell's theorem
standard_prerequisites.statement: For a Poisson process with mean measure mu and a measurable f, the Laplace transform of the sum of f over the points is the exponential of the integral of e to the s f minus one against mu, whenever the integral converges.
standard_prerequisites.use: It supplies the moment generating function computed in the proof.

standard_prerequisites.name: Exponential distribution
standard_prerequisites.statement: A positive random variable with moment generating function t/(t-s) for s below t is exponentially distributed with parameter t.
standard_prerequisites.use: It converts the computed generating function into the asserted law.

core_obligations: Apply Campbell's theorem to the scale-invariant process with the exponential test function to compute the moment generating function of I_t as t/(t-s) for the real part of s below t (source line 820).
Recognise that expression as the moment generating function of the exponential distribution of parameter t, which gives the tail formula stated (source line 820).

proof_roadmap.step: Compute the moment generating function of I_t by Campbell's theorem.
Identify it with the moment generating function of the exponential law of parameter t.

difficulty_reason: Counted unit is the author's labelled proposition at source lines 814-817, attributed by the author to Arratia: for every fixed positive t the random variable I_t is exponentially distributed with parameter t. The proof (source lines 819-821) is a one-step application of Campbell's theorem, but the step is substantive: the theorem has to be applied to the scale-invariant process with an exponential test function, giving the moment generating function t/(t-s) on the half-plane where the defining integral converges, and that expression has to be recognised as the moment generating function of the exponential law of parameter t in order to conclude the tail formula. The statement records the law and neither the transform computation nor the convergence condition on s.
